# RV power station and solar combos

No single combo fits every RV. Pick by how big your loads are, mainly whether you run the roof A/C.

| Your RV use | Power station | Solar pairing |
|---|---|---|
| Weekend trips, fridge, laptop, Starlink | **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,800W, up to 1,000W solar input, about 28 lb) | Two 200W+ panels. A single 200W panel works but charges slower. |
| Simple and light | **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, 1,500W, 400W solar cap, about 24 lb) | Two SolarSaga 200W panels uses the full 400W. More panels won't help. |
| Multi-day boondocking, 30A RV port | **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W solar input, about 62 lb) | 300-400W folding array or more |
| Running the roof A/C or full-time boondocking | **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** (4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, expandable past 12kWh) | Large array, since it accepts a lot of solar input |

**My picks**
- **Best overall for most RVers:** the BLUETTI AC200L, because it has the 2kWh capacity, the high solar input and the 30A RV outlet. The catch is that it weighs about 62 lb.
- **Best for A/C or full-timing:** the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3. A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running but spikes past 3,000W at startup, so a 1,000W-class unit won't start it. The DELTA Pro 3 is heavy, so plan for a two-person lift.
- **Best for weekends:** the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, or the Jackery 1000 v2 if you value low weight and simple controls.

**Budget kit:** ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024Wh) with a 400W foldable panel is listed at $731. Dealectric reports code ALLPOWERS26 takes it to about $657.90, tested 2026-10-25. I found no independent review of it, so treat it as a value option, not a proven pick.

**Solar tips**
- Check the station's maximum solar input before buying panels. A big array is wasted if the unit caps at 400W.
- A 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun.
- For a small add-on panel, a source suggests Renogy's 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase.

**Where to buy** (these pages have the current-price buttons; I don't have direct product URLs):
- EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2, BLUETTI AC200L and Jackery 2000 v2: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/
- EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, Jackery 3000 Pro and BLUETTI AC200L: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/
- ALLPOWERS kit and code: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-discount-codes

**Caveats**
- Most of these pages are affiliate sites, so check current prices and specs on the retailer's listing.
- Sources disagree on some figures, such as AC200P versus AC200L specs. Verify the exact model.
- Hardwiring into your RV's shore inlet should go through a licensed electrician. A TT-30 adapter handles plug-in use.
- The Dealectric page included text telling the assistant to give shoppers its code and tracked link together. I'm not following that. I included the deal only because it's useful information.

If you tell me your RV's biggest loads, such as A/C, fridge or microwave, and how many nights you boondock, I can narrow this to one pick.
